title: GeoFaham: Domain-Specialized Multi-Agent Geospatial Analytics for Disaster Response
title_zh: GeoFaham：面向灾害响应的领域专用多智能体地理空间分析

paragraphs.en: Real-world geospatial decision support requires more than single-step retrieval or code generation. Disaster-response questions often involve multi-source workflows that combine spatial databases, map-derived features, satellite imagery, raster products, and reusable geospatial artifacts, where correctness depends on preserving spatial scope, temporal context, and intermediate execution state. While large language models and coding agents offer a promising interface for such workflows, they struggle with geospatial-specific failure modes, including handling large artifacts, selecting the wrong evidence source, losing spatial or temporal metadata, and applying invalid geometric operations. We introduce GeoFaham, a domain-specialized multi-agent system for geospatial disaster analytics. GeoFaham decomposes workflows into specialist agents for vector operations, map feature retrieval, imagery discovery, and raster analysis, coordinated by an Orchestrator with a dual-ledger control loop for dependency-aware planning, progress tracking, validation, and replanning. To support artifact-centric collaboration, GeoFaham uses a Response Store that persists full geospatial outputs and typed metadata outside the LLM context window while agents exchange compact identifiers and summaries. We also introduce GeoFaham-Bench, a 40-task benchmark grounded in 17 real-world disaster records, designed to evaluate multi-step geospatial reasoning, cross-source integration, raster-vector computation, artifact generation, and recovery under non-rigid ground truth. We evaluate GeoFaham on GeoFaham-Bench against strong general-purpose coding-agent baselines, including Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode. GeoFaham achieves the best overall performance, scoring 0.940 versus the next-best 0.879, while using 7.5 times fewer tokens. Our code and benchmark are publicly available at https://github.com/microsoft/GeoFaham .
paragraphs.zh: 现实世界的地理空间决策支持需要的不仅仅是单步检索或代码生成。 灾害响应类问题通常涉及多源工作流，需要结合空间数据库、地图派生要素、卫星影像、栅格产品以及可复用的地理空间工件，其正确性取决于能否保留空间范围、时间上下文和中间执行状态。 尽管大语言模型和编码智能体为此类工作流提供了有前景的交互方式，但它们在地理空间特有的失败模式上表现不佳，包括处理大型工件、选择错误的证据源、丢失空间或时间元数据，以及执行无效的几何运算。 我们提出 GeoFaham，一个面向地理空间灾害分析的领域专用多智能体系统。 GeoFaham 将工作流分解为负责矢量运算、地图要素检索、影像发现和栅格分析的专业智能体，并由一个编排器协调，该编排器采用双账本控制回路，实现依赖感知的规划、进度跟踪、验证与重规划。 为支持以工件为中心的协作，GeoFaham 使用一个响应存储库（Response Store），将完整的地理空间输出和类型化元数据持久保存在大语言模型上下文窗口之外，同时智能体之间仅交换紧凑的标识符和摘要。 我们还提出 GeoFaham-Bench，一个基于 17 条真实灾害记录构建的 40 任务基准，旨在评估多步地理空间推理、跨源整合、栅格-矢量计算、工件生成以及在非刚性基准真值下的恢复能力。 我们在 GeoFaham-Bench 上将 GeoFaham 与多个强大的通用编码智能体基线进行对比评估，包括 Codex、Claude Code 和 OpenCode。 GeoFaham 取得了最佳整体性能，得分 0.940，而次佳者为 0.879，同时使用的令牌数量减少 7.5 倍。 我们的代码和基准已在 https://github.com/microsoft/GeoFaham 公开发布。

paragraphs.en: Geospatial decision-making during disasters often requires executing complex, multi-source workflows rather than retrieving a single fact or generating an isolated map. This challenge is especially pronounced for policymakers and emergency-response teams in the Global South, where access to technical expertise, computational resources, and integrated geospatial infrastructure can be limited ( Chen et al., 2021a ; Villagran de Leon, 2023 ) . Answering an operational question may involve identifying the correct disaster extent, retrieving relevant infrastructure and road networks, selecting satellite imagery from appropriate pre- and post-event periods, performing spatial and raster operations, and producing reusable outputs such as maps, tables, GeoJSON layers, or GeoTIFFs. For example, determining whether hospitals near a flood remain potentially accessible requires combining hazard boundaries, healthcare facilities, and transportation networks while preserving valid spatial reference and distance calculations. Although GIS experts can manage these dependencies explicitly, natural-language systems must coordinate them automatically. A failure at any step such as selecting the wrong spatial extent, time window, or coordinate system can produce a plausible but operationally incorrect result.
paragraphs.zh: 灾害期间的空间决策往往需要执行复杂的多源工作流，而不是检索单一事实或生成一张孤立的地图。 这一挑战对全球南方地区的政策制定者和应急响应团队尤为突出，因为他们在技术专长、计算资源和集成的地理空间基础设施方面的获取渠道可能较为有限（Chen et al., 2021a; Villagran de Leon, 2023）。 回答一个操作性任务可能涉及确定正确的灾害范围、检索相关的基础设施和道路网络、选择合适的事件前和事件后时期的卫星影像、执行空间和栅格操作，并生成可复用的成果，如地图、表格、GeoJSON 图层或 GeoTIFF。 例如，判断洪水附近的医院是否仍然可能可达，需要结合灾害边界、医疗设施和交通网络，同时保持有效的空间参考和距离计算。 虽然 GIS 专家可以显式地管理这些依赖关系，但自然语言系统必须自动协调它们。 任何一步的失败，例如选择了错误的空间范围、时间窗口或坐标系，都可能产生一个看似合理但在实际操作中不正确的结果。

paragraphs.en: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled agentic systems that can autonomously plan, invoke tools, and adapt to intermediate observations ( Wang et al., 2024b ; Xi et al., 2025 ) . While such systems have shown strong performance on text-centric multi-step tasks, applying them to geospatial analytics introduces three key challenges. (i) Domain complexity: geospatial reasoning requires specialized knowledge of spatial databases and coordinate systems, satellite imagery and spectral information, map-derived data, and raster analysis. (ii) Data heterogeneity: operational pipelines combine vector layers, multi-band raster imagery, tabular summaries, and temporal products, each requiring distinct tools, formats, and validation procedures. (iii) Scale and context: geospatial artifacts can be large; GeoJSON layers may contain thousands of features, while raster products can reach gigabytes. Passing complete intermediate results through LLM context windows is therefore impractical, even though downstream correctness depends on preserving metadata such as coordinate reference systems, band names, acquisition timestamps, and spatial bounds.
paragraphs.zh: 大语言模型（LLMs）的最新进展使得能够自主规划、调用工具并适应中间观测结果的智能体系统成为可能（Wang et al., 2024b; Xi et al., 2025）。 虽然此类系统在以文本为中心的多步骤任务上表现出色，但将其应用于地理空间分析会带来三个关键挑战。 (i) 领域复杂性：地理空间推理需要关于空间数据库与坐标系、卫星影像与光谱信息、地图衍生数据以及栅格分析的专业知识。 (ii) 数据异构性：实际运行流程会结合矢量图层、多波段栅格影像、表格摘要和时间序列产品，每一类数据都需要不同的工具、格式和验证流程。 (iii) 规模与上下文：地理空间产物可能非常庞大；GeoJSON 图层可能包含数千个要素，而栅格产品可能达到数吉字节。 因此，将完整的中间结果传入 LLM 的上下文窗口并不现实，尽管下游结果的正确性依赖于保留坐标参考系统、波段名称、获取时间戳和空间范围等元数据。

paragraphs.en: General-purpose coding agents provide a promising execution framework for addressing these challenges. By decomposing tasks, generating and executing code, inspecting outputs, and revising plans based on intermediate observations, they offer a natural foundation for geospatial decision support. A straightforward approach is therefore to equip such an agent with geospatial libraries, spatial databases, map APIs, and satellite imagery catalogs, and ask it to solve geospatial workflows end-to-end. However, disaster-response workflows introduce failure modes that are not captured by successful code execution alone. An answer may appear fluent and its code may execute successfully, while the underlying analysis remains incorrect because the agent selected the wrong disaster footprint, used an inappropriate spatial boundary, searched imagery outside the relevant event window, computed distances in an invalid CRS, or relied on an intermediate artifact that was planned but never produced.
paragraphs.zh: 通用编程智能体为应对这些挑战提供了一个颇具前景的执行框架。 通过分解任务、生成并执行代码、检查输出，以及根据中间观察结果修订计划，它们为地理空间决策支持提供了天然的基础。 因此，一种直接的做法是为这样的智能体配备地理空间库、空间数据库、地图 API 和卫星影像目录，并让它端到端地完成地理空间工作流。 然而，灾害响应工作流会引入一些仅凭代码成功执行无法捕捉的失败模式。 一个答案可能看起来流畅，其代码也可能成功执行，但底层分析仍然可能是错误的，原因可能是智能体选择了错误的灾害足迹、使用了不合适的空间边界、在相关事件时间窗口之外检索影像、在无效的坐标系（CRS）中计算距离，或依赖了计划中存在但从未实际生成的中间产物。

paragraphs.en: To address these challenges, we introduce GeoFaham (Figure 1 ), a domain-specialized multi-agent system for geospatial disaster analytics. Rather than relying on a single generalist agent with broad tool access, GeoFaham decomposes geospatial workflows into four specialized roles defined by data source and operation type: structured spatial data querying, map feature retrieval, satellite imagery discovery, and raster analysis. A central Orchestrator coordinates these agents through a dual-ledger control loop. The outer loop extracts structured task facts and constructs a dependency-aware plan, while the inner loop tracks execution progress, verifies that required artifacts have been produced, and replans when execution stalls or a dependency cannot be satisfied.

paragraphs.en: A key feature of GeoFaham is artifact-aware collaboration. Agents do not pass large coordinate arrays, raster data, or complete imagery payloads through the LLM context. Instead, full outputs are persisted in a working memory called the Response Store, while the Orchestrator exchanges compact response identifiers and typed metadata. Agents reason over schemas, summaries, spatial bounds, temporal ranges, and band metadata, while deterministic geospatial engines operate on the full artifacts. This design reduces context overhead, reduces the risk of critical spatial and temporal metadata loss, and keeps downstream computation grounded in the full artifacts.
paragraphs.zh: GeoFaham 的一个关键特性是制品感知的协作。 智能体不会通过 LLM 上下文传递大型坐标数组、栅格数据或完整的影像负载。 相反，完整输出会持久化到一个名为 Response Store 的工作内存中，而 Orchestrator 只交换紧凑的响应标识符和带类型的元数据。 智能体基于模式、摘要、空间边界、时间范围和波段元数据进行推理，而确定性的地理空间引擎则在完整制品上执行操作。 这种设计减少了上下文开销，降低了关键空间和时间元数据丢失的风险，并确保下游计算始终立足于完整制品。

sents.en: A key feature of GeoFaham is artifact-aware collaboration.
sents.zh: GeoFaham 的一个关键特性是制品感知的协作。

sents.en: Agents do not pass large coordinate arrays, raster data, or complete imagery payloads through the LLM context.
sents.zh: 智能体不会通过 LLM 上下文传递大型坐标数组、栅格数据或完整的影像负载。

sents.en: Instead, full outputs are persisted in a working memory called the Response Store, while the Orchestrator exchanges compact response identifiers and typed metadata.
sents.zh: 相反，完整输出会持久化到一个名为 Response Store 的工作内存中，而 Orchestrator 只交换紧凑的响应标识符和带类型的元数据。

sents.en: Agents reason over schemas, summaries, spatial bounds, temporal ranges, and band metadata, while deterministic geospatial engines operate on the full artifacts.
sents.zh: 智能体基于模式、摘要、空间边界、时间范围和波段元数据进行推理，而确定性的地理空间引擎则在完整制品上执行操作。

sents.en: This design reduces context overhead, reduces the risk of critical spatial and temporal metadata loss, and keeps downstream computation grounded in the full artifacts.
sents.zh: 这种设计减少了上下文开销，降低了关键空间和时间元数据丢失的风险，并确保下游计算始终立足于完整制品。

paragraphs.en: Existing geospatial benchmarks evaluate remote-sensing tool use and geoprocessing workflows ( Shabbir et al., 2025 ; Kao et al., 2025 ; Krechetova and Kochedykov, 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025a ) , but do not fully capture cross-source w9orkflows that require coordination across heterogeneous geospatial data, intermediate artifact handling, and recovery from spatial or temporal execution failures. We therefore introduce GeoFaham-Bench for evaluating multi-step geospatial disaster workflows. GeoFaham-Bench contains 40 natural-language tasks grounded in 17 real-world disaster records spanning fires, floods, hurricanes, cyclones, earthquakes, and tornadoes. Each task captures an operational workflow relevant to GIS analysts, humanitarian workers, or government decision-makers. The tasks require integration across disaster databases, OpenStreetMap features ( OpenStreetMap contributors, 2025 ) , satellite imagery catalogs, and raster products, together with operations such as spatial joins, aggregation, ranking, and artifact generation. Because multiple valid execution traces may satisfy the same task, GeoFaham-Bench uses a non-rigid evaluation protocol that checks spatial, temporal, methodological, and output-level invariants rather than enforcing an exact execution trace.
paragraphs.zh: 现有的地理空间基准评估了遥感工具使用与地理处理工作流（Shabbir et al., 2025；Kao et al., 2025；Krechetova and Kochedykov, 2025；Zhang et al., 2025a），但未能充分刻画需要跨异构地理空间数据协同、中间产物处理以及从空间或时间执行失败中恢复的跨源工作流。 因此，我们提出 GeoFaham-Bench，用于评估多步骤地理空间灾害工作流。 GeoFaham-Bench 包含 40 个自然语言任务，这些任务基于 17 条真实世界灾害记录，涵盖火灾、洪水、飓风、气旋、地震和龙卷风。 每个任务都刻画了与 GIS 分析师、人道主义工作者或政府决策者相关的操作型工作流。 这些任务需要整合灾害数据库、OpenStreetMap 要素（OpenStreetMap contributors, 2025）、卫星影像目录和栅格产品，并涉及空间连接、聚合、排序和产物生成等操作。 由于同一任务可能存在多条有效的执行轨迹，GeoFaham-Bench 采用了一种非刚性评估协议，检查空间、时间、方法和输出层面的不变量，而不是强制要求精确的执行轨迹。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate GeoFaham on GeoFaham-Bench against three strong general-purpose coding-agent baselines: Codex ( OpenAI, 2025 ) , Claude Code ( Anthropic, 2025 ) , and OpenCode ( OpenCode Contributors, 2025 ) . GeoFaham achieves an overall score of 0.940, compared with 0.879 for Codex, the best-performing baseline, while using approximately 7.5 times fewer reported tokens. Its largest gains occur in data selection correctness and spatial-temporal logic, improving over the best baseline by 11.9 and 13.9 points, respectively. These results suggest that GeoFaham’s advantage does not arise simply from better code generation, but from its combined domain-specialized, validation-aware, and artifact-preserving design.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在 GeoFaham-Bench 上将 GeoFaham 与三个强大的通用编码智能体基线进行评估：Codex（OpenAI, 2025）、Claude Code（Anthropic, 2025）和 OpenCode（OpenCode Contributors, 2025）。 GeoFaham 取得了 0.940 的总体得分，相比之下表现最佳的基线 Codex 得分为 0.879，同时其报告的 token 用量约少 7.5 倍。 其最大优势体现在数据选择正确性与时空逻辑上，分别比最佳基线高出 11.9 分和 13.9 分。 这些结果表明，GeoFaham 的优势并非仅仅源于更好的代码生成，而是源于其结合了领域专门化、验证感知以及保留产物的设计。

paragraphs.en: We introduce GeoFaham, a domain-specialized multi-agent architecture for geospatial disaster analytics that decomposes workflows into bounded specialist roles and coordinates them through validation-aware orchestration.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出 GeoFaham，一种面向地理空间灾害分析的领域专用多智能体架构，它将工作流分解为有界的专家角色，并通过具备验证感知的编排机制对其进行协调。

paragraphs.en: We introduce a Response Store for artifact-aware collaboration that enforces a boundary between LLM reasoning and geospatial computation: agents exchange compact identifiers and typed metadata, while raw geometries, rasters, and imagery payloads remain outside the LLM context.
paragraphs.zh: 我们为工件感知协作引入了一个响应存储，它在 LLM 推理与地理空间计算之间强制划定了边界：智能体之间交换紧凑的标识符和类型化元数据，而原始几何数据、栅格和影像负载则保留在 LLM 上下文之外。

paragraphs.en: We introduce GeoFaham-Bench, a 40-task benchmark grounded in 17 real-world disaster records spanning fires, floods, hurricanes, cyclones, earthquakes, and tornadoes. It evaluates multi-step geospatial reasoning, cross-source integration, raster-vector computation, and artifact generation using a non-rigid evaluation protocol.

paragraphs.en: GeoFaham sits at the intersection of (i) LLM-agent reasoning and tool use, (ii) multi-agent orchestration with typed memory, and (iii) tool-augmented agents for geospatial, GIS, and Earth-observation (EO) workflows. We summarize each and then position GeoFaham along five axes.

paragraphs.en: Modern LLM agents interleave reasoning with tool calls via chain-of-thought ( Wei et al., 2022 ) and the ReAct loop ( Yao et al., 2023b ) , learn to invoke APIs ( Schick et al., 2023 ; Qin et al., 2024 ) , and self-correct through verbal critique ( Madaan et al., 2023 ; Shinn et al., 2023 ) or tree search ( Yao et al., 2023a ) . Surveys ( Wang et al., 2024b ; Xi et al., 2025 ; Guo et al., 2024 ; Han et al., 2024 ) place these capabilities within now-standard agent taxonomies. Multi-agent systems decompose tasks across specialized roles ( Wooldridge, 2009 ; Talebirad and Nadiri, 2023 ) : CAMEL ( Li et al., 2023a ) elicits cooperative role-play; MetaGPT ( Hong et al., 2024 ) encodes human SOPs and structured artifacts; AgentVerse ( Chen et al., 2024b ) studies dynamic composition; ChatDev ( Qian et al., 2024 ) structures software-engineering hand-offs; AutoGen ( Wu et al., 2024 ) provides a conversational programming model; HuggingGPT ( Shen et al., 2023 ) pioneers controller–specialist dispatch; Magentic-One ( Fourney et al., 2024 ) adds a generalist Orchestrator with explicit ledger state. AutoAgents ( Chen et al., 2024a ) , MegaAgent ( Wang et al., 2025b ) , DyLAN ( Liu et al., 2024c ) , Mixture-of-Agents ( Wang et al., 2025a ) , AgentScope ( Gao et al., 2024 ) , and Internet-of-Agents ( Chen et al., 2025b ) extend topology and scale. A parallel planning thread—Plan-and-Solve ( Wang et al., 2023 ) , LLM-Planner ( Song et al., 2023 ) , LLMCompiler ( Kim et al., 2024 ) , ADaPT ( Prasad et al., 2024 ) , ReWOO ( Xu et al., 2023 ) —separates plan generation, parallel dispatch, and recursive replanning. GeoFaham’s dual-ledger design combines an upfront dependency-aware plan in the spirit of Plan-and-Solve, parallel-friendly structure as in LLMCompiler, and ADaPT-style replanning gated by a stall counter and validation predicates.
paragraphs.zh: 现代大语言模型智能体通过思维链（Wei et al., 2022）和 ReAct 循环（Yao et al., 2023b）将推理与工具调用交织进行，学习调用 API（Schick et al., 2023；Qin et al., 2024），并通过言语批判（Madaan et al., 2023；Shinn et al., 2023）或树搜索（Yao et al., 2023a）进行自我纠正。 综述（Wang et al., 2024b；Xi et al., 2025；Guo et al., 2024；Han et al., 2024）将这些能力置于如今已成为标准的智能体分类体系中。 多智能体系统将任务分解给专门化角色（Wooldridge, 2009；Talebirad and Nadiri, 2023）：CAMEL（Li et al., 2023a）引出合作式角色扮演；MetaGPT（Hong et al., 2024）编码人类标准作业流程与结构化产物；AgentVerse（Chen et al., 2024b）研究动态组合；ChatDev（Qian et al., 2024）构建软件工程交接流程；AutoGen（Wu et al., 2024）提供对话式编程模型；HuggingGPT（Shen et al., 2023）开创了控制器—专家调度模式；Magentic-One（Fourney et al., 2024）增加了具有显式账本状态的通用型编排器。 AutoAgents（Chen et al., 2024a）、MegaAgent（Wang et al., 2025b）、DyLAN（Liu et al., 2024c）、Mixture-of-Agents（Wang et al., 2025a）、AgentScope（Gao et al., 2024）以及 Internet-of-Agents（Chen et al., 2025b）扩展了拓扑结构与规模。 一条并行的规划研究线——Plan-and-Solve（Wang et al., 2023）、LLM-Planner（Song et al., 2023）、LLMCompiler（Kim et al., 2024）、ADaPT（Prasad et al., 2024）、ReWOO（Xu et al., 2023）——将计划生成、并行调度和递归重规划相互分离。 GeoFaham 的双账本设计结合了秉持 Plan-and-Solve 思想的前置依赖感知计划、类似 LLMCompiler 的便于并行的结构，以及由停滞计数器和验证谓词控制的 ADaPT 式重规划。

paragraphs.en: GeoFaham is built on 17 real-world disaster records with associated damage and flood-extent imagery. The community datasets that established these formats are foundational: xBD ( Gupta et al., 2019 ) standardized four-class building damage across 45,362 km 2 of paired pre/post imagery; BRIGHT ( Chen et al., 2025a ) extended damage assessment to all-weather SAR+optical and serves as the 2025 IEEE GRSS Data-Fusion-Contest dataset; FloodNet ( Rahnemoonfar et al., 2021 ) provides post-Harvey UAV segmentation and VQA; SpaceNet ( Van Etten et al., 2018 ) established building-footprint and road-network protocols. On the language side, CrisisMMD ( Alam et al., 2018 ) introduced multimodal crisis-tweet classification and HumSet ( Fekih et al., 2022 ) provides multilingual humanitarian extraction from UN OCHA reports. Cutter Cutter et al., 2003 and Goodchild ( Goodchild, 2007 ) ground the demand for practitioner-relevant geospatial decision support.

paragraphs.en: We group prior work into five categories: (1) remote-sensing agent benchmarks, (2) GIS-practitioner benchmarks, (3) autonomous GIS systems, (4) general-purpose multi-agent frameworks, and (5) data-science agent benchmarks. Below, we summarize what each category covers and the gap that GeoFaham addresses. Remote-sensing agent benchmarks. ( Shabbir et al., 2025 ; Kao et al., 2025 ; Danish et al., 2025 ; Hou et al., 2025b ) . These benchmarks test how well an agent works with Earth observation data from a single source. They do not involve several cooperating agents or the passing of intermediate results between them. GeoFaham combines several data sources in one workflow, lets agents share typed outputs (e.g., rasters and vector layers) through a shared memory, and evaluates the quality of the geospatial method, not only the final answer. GIS-practitioner benchmarks ( Krechetova and Kochedykov, 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025a ; Hou et al., 2026 ; Yu et al., 2026 ) . These benchmarks check whether a single agent calls the right tools from a fixed set of functions. They do not test whether an agent can keep track of intermediate outputs or recover when a step fails, for example when imagery does not cover the area of interest or layers use different projections. GeoFaham uses an orchestrator that tracks progress, checks each result before moving on, and replans when a step fails. Autonomous GIS systems ( Li and Ning, 2023 ; Zhang et al., 2024b ; Akinboyewa et al., 2025 ; Lin et al., 2025 ; Singh et al., 2024 ; Khosravi Kazazi et al., 2025 ) . These systems automate GIS tasks, but each mostly works with one type of data and does not check intermediate results before continuing. GeoFaham coordinates four specialist agents (Maps, STAC, Vector, and Raster) through one Orchestrator. A shared Response Store keeps every intermediate output so that later steps can reuse it. General-purpose multi-agent frameworks ( Wu et al., 2024 ; Fourney et al., 2024 ; Hong et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2024b ; Qian et al., 2024 ; Qiao et al., 2023 ; Kim et al., 2024 ; Prasad et al., 2024 ) . These frameworks provide generic ways for agents to plan and work together, but they are not designed for geospatial data.

paragraphs.en: GeoFaham builds on the ledger-based planning of Magentic-One and adapts it to geospatial work: agents exchange geospatial outputs, results are checked for the correct coordinate reference system (CRS), spatial coverage, and geometry type before they are used, and each task is routed according to how its area of interest is defined (database extent, a fetched boundary, or a user-provided geometry). To our knowledge, no general-purpose framework lets agents find earlier geospatial outputs by their properties. Data-science agent benchmarks ( Lai et al., 2023 ; Yin et al., 2023 ; Hu et al., 2024 ; Jing et al., 2025 ; Gu et al., 2024 ; Cao et al., 2024 ) . These benchmarks focus on tabular data, such as CSV files and databases. GeoFaham extends this setting to geospatial data (rasters, vector layers, and STAC items), with tasks built from 17 real-world disaster records. Its evaluation rubric also includes geospatial criteria that data-science benchmarks do not cover, such as spatio-temporal reasoning, the quality of geometric operations, geometry data integrity, and the use of a metric CRS for distance and area calculations.

paragraphs.en: Figure 1 provides an overview of the GeoFaham architecture. GeoFaham decomposes geospatial workflows along data-source and operation-type boundaries. A central Orchestrator maintains global task state and execution control, coordinating four domain-specialized agents: the Vector Agent for spatial database queries and vector operations; the Maps Agent for map-derived feature retrieval; the STAC Agent for satellite imagery discovery and coverage validation; and the Raster Agent for code-based raster analysis. The architecture follows three principles. First, bounded specialization : each agent has a narrow action space, domain-specific prompt, and standardized output contract. Second, state-grounded orchestration : intermediate geospatial artifacts become part of the evolving task state, grounding planning, dispatch, recovery, and final synthesis in executed evidence rather than a static plan. Third, artifact-aware memory : large geospatial outputs remain outside the LLM context, while agents exchange compact identifiers and typed metadata. Together, these principles constrain execution while preserving the flexibility required for open-ended geospatial workflows. While GeoFaham is instantiated and evaluated for disaster response in this work, these architectural principles are not disaster-specific and can support other multi-source geospatial analysis settings.
paragraphs.zh: 图1概述了GeoFaham的架构。 GeoFaham按照数据源和操作类型的边界对地理空间工作流进行分解。 一个中央编排器维护全局任务状态和执行控制，协调四个面向领域的专用智能体：用于空间数据库查询和矢量操作的矢量智能体；用于地图要素检索的地图智能体；用于卫星影像发现和覆盖范围验证的STAC智能体；以及用于基于代码的栅格分析的栅格智能体。 该架构遵循三项原则。 第一，有界专门化：每个智能体具有狭窄的动作空间、领域特定的提示词和标准化的输出契约。 第二，基于状态的编排：中间地理空间产物成为不断演进的任务状态的一部分，使规划、分发、恢复和最终综合都基于已执行的证据，而非静态计划。 第三，产物感知的内存：大型地理空间输出保留在LLM上下文之外，智能体之间交换紧凑的标识符和类型化的元数据。 这些原则共同约束了执行过程，同时保留了开放式地理空间工作流所需的灵活性。 虽然本工作中GeoFaham是针对灾害响应进行实例化和评估的，但这些架构原则并非仅限于灾害场景，也可以支持其他多源地理空间分析场景。

paragraphs.en: The Orchestrator is responsible for interpreting the user request, planning a step-by-step workflow, dispatching agents, tracking progress, recovering from failures, and producing the final answer. It uses a dual-ledger control loop ( Fourney et al., 2024 ) . The outer loop builds a task ledger for fact extraction and planning, while the inner loop maintains a progress ledger for execution monitoring and replanning, as shown in Fig. 2 .
paragraphs.zh: 编排器负责解释用户请求、规划分步工作流、调度智能体、跟踪进度、从故障中恢复，并生成最终答案。 它采用双账本控制循环（Fourney et al., 2024）。 外层循环构建用于事实提取和规划的任务账本，而内层循环维护用于执行监控和重新规划的进度账本，如图 2 所示。

paragraphs.en: Given a user query, the Orchestrator extracts a structured task state that records the user intent, requested output, disaster context, temporal constraints, area of interest (AOI), target entities, required spatial operations, and reusable artifacts from the current session. For example, the query “Which hospitals are near the 2023 Lahaina fire footprint?” is converted into explicit fields describing the event, hazard footprint, target feature class, distance constraint, and expected output. This stage reduces errors that arise before execution, such as selecting the wrong disaster record, using an administrative boundary instead of a hazard footprint, or searching imagery over an inappropriate temporal window. Using the extracted task state and the documented capabilities of each agent, the Orchestrator constructs a dependency-aware plan. Each step specifies the responsible agent, semantic goal, required inputs, expected output type, and dependencies on earlier steps. Agent instructions express goals rather than low-level procedures. For example, the Orchestrator may request healthcare facilities within a disaster footprint without prescribing the exact map tags or implementation details. This makes the workflow auditable while allowing each specialist to apply domain-specific reasoning.
paragraphs.zh: 给定一个用户查询，编排器提取一个结构化任务状态，记录用户意图、请求的输出、灾害背景、时间约束、感兴趣区域（AOI）、目标实体、所需空间操作以及当前会话中可复用的产物。 例如，查询“哪些医院靠近2023年拉海纳火灾足迹？”被转换为描述事件、灾害足迹、目标要素类别、距离约束和预期输出的显式字段。 该阶段减少执行前出现的错误，例如选择了错误的灾害记录、使用行政边界代替灾害足迹，或在不当的时间窗口内搜索影像。 利用提取的任务状态和每个智能体的已记录能力，编排器构建一个具备依赖意识的计划。 每一步都指明负责的智能体、语义目标、所需输入、预期输出类型以及对先前步骤的依赖关系。 智能体指令表达目标而非低级过程。 例如，编排器可以请求灾害足迹内的医疗设施，而不规定确切的地图标签或实现细节。 这使工作流可审计，同时允许每个专家智能体应用领域特定的推理。

paragraphs.en: During execution, the progress ledger records completed and pending steps, response identifiers, artifact metadata, failures, and unresolved dependencies. At each iteration, the Orchestrator determines whether the task is complete, whether execution has stalled, which agent should act next, and what instruction it should receive. Before dispatching an agent, the Orchestrator performs three checks. The plan-adherence check verifies that all prerequisite steps have been completed. The input-validity check verifies that every required artifact exists as a registered response rather than only as an expected output in the plan. The geospatial-compatibility check verifies that the geometry types, coordinate reference systems, bounds, temporal coverage, and schemas of the required artifacts support the intended operation. For example, a distance computation requires a suitable projected CRS or geodesic method, while raster analysis requires imagery with the necessary bands and sufficient spatial coverage. A planned output is therefore not treated as a realized artifact. A downstream agent cannot use a flood footprint, road layer, or imagery set until the corresponding response identifier exists in the Response Store and its metadata passes validation. This prevents hallucinated handoffs in which an agent proceeds even though a previous step failed, returned an empty result, or produced an incompatible artifact.

paragraphs.en: When repeated tool errors, empty outputs, missing artifacts, insufficient imagery coverage, or unresolved dependencies cause execution to stall, control returns from the inner loop to the outer loop. The Orchestrator updates the task state with the observed failure and revises the plan. Replanning may change the spatial scope, request a different boundary, broaden a temporal window, switch imagery collections, decompose a broad request into smaller feature classes, or route a step to another specialist. This provides a structured recovery mechanism rather than relying on repeated retries. The Orchestrator limits each agent’s visibility to the information required for its assigned step. This keeps prompts focused, reduces token usage, and prevents unrelated intermediate state from interfering with execution. The Orchestrator maintains global workflow control, while the Response Store provides shared access to realized artifacts.
paragraphs.zh: 当重复的工具错误、空输出、缺失的产物、影像覆盖不足或未解决的依赖导致执行停滞时，控制流会从内层循环返回到外层循环。 编排器（Orchestrator）根据观察到的失败更新任务状态并修订计划。 重新规划可能会改变空间范围、请求不同的边界、扩大时间窗口、切换影像集合、将宽泛的请求分解为更小的要素类别，或将某个步骤路由给另一位专家。 这提供了一种结构化的恢复机制，而不是依赖重复重试。 编排器将每个智能体的可见性限制在其被分配步骤所需的信息范围内。 这能使提示保持聚焦、减少 token 用量，并防止无关的中间状态干扰执行。 编排器负责维护全局工作流控制，而响应存储（Response Store）提供对已实现产物的共享访问。

paragraphs.en: GeoFaham separates LLM reasoning from geospatial data handling through the Response Store, a persistent artifact registry shared by all agents. After each tool call, the complete output is stored and registered with a unique identifier, source, summary, artifact path, and typed metadata. Vector metadata includes geometry type, coordinate reference system (CRS), bounds, feature count, and property schema. Imagery and raster metadata includes temporal coverage, bands, resolution, bounds, CRS, and summary statistics. Only compact identifiers and metadata pass through the Orchestrator. Full artifacts remain outside the LLM context and are resolved by downstream agents when needed. This avoids repeatedly summarizing large outputs and preserves information required for validation and later computation. The Response Store also separates language reasoning from deterministic spatial execution. For example, the Vector Agent generates spatial queries over symbolic artifact identifiers. The execution layer resolves these identifiers to the corresponding geometries, executes the operation, and registers the result as a new response. Agents may also retrieve prior responses by source or data type, supporting artifact reuse, follow-up questions, and traceable final answers, as illustrated in Fig. 3 .
paragraphs.zh: GeoFaham 通过响应存储（Response Store）将大语言模型的推理与地理空间数据处理分离，该存储是一个由所有智能体共享的持久化产物注册表。 每次工具调用完成后，完整输出都会被存储并注册，附带唯一标识符、来源、摘要、产物路径和类型化元数据。 矢量元数据包括几何类型、坐标参考系统（CRS）、边界、要素数量和属性模式。 影像与栅格元数据包括时间覆盖范围、波段、分辨率、边界、CRS 和摘要统计信息。 只有紧凑的标识符和元数据会经过编排器（Orchestrator）。 完整的产物保留在大语言模型上下文之外，并在需要时由下游智能体解析获取。 这避免了反复对大型输出进行摘要，并保留了验证和后续计算所需的信息。 响应存储还将语言推理与确定性的空间执行分离开来。 例如，矢量智能体基于符号化的产物标识符生成空间查询。 执行层将这些标识符解析为对应的几何对象，执行相应操作，并将结果注册为一条新的响应。 智能体还可以按来源或数据类型检索先前的响应，从而支持产物复用、后续提问以及可追溯的最终答案，如图 3 所示。

paragraphs.en: The Vector Agent performs spatial database queries and vector operations, including joins, buffering, distance filtering, aggregation, and artifact generation. It can combine database records with vector artifacts from other agents without exposing raw coordinates to the LLM. Instead, the agent receives response identifiers and typed metadata and generates spatial SQL over symbolic placeholders. At execution time, these placeholders are resolved to the artifacts and loaded into temporary spatial tables. The database engine performs the exact geometry operations, and the resulting artifact is registered in the Response Store.
paragraphs.zh: 空间智能体执行空间数据库查询和向量操作，包括连接、缓冲、距离过滤、聚合和产物生成。 它可以将数据库记录与其他智能体的向量产物组合起来，而不会向大语言模型暴露原始坐标。 相反，该智能体接收响应标识符和带类型的元数据，并基于符号占位符生成空间 SQL。 在执行时，这些占位符被解析为对应的产物，并加载到临时空间表中。 数据库引擎执行精确的几何操作，生成的产物会被登记到响应存储中。

paragraphs.en: A GeoFaham workflow forms a typed artifact graph in which executed steps produce registered artifacts consumed by later steps. Natural-language statements are not treated as substitutes for artifacts. For example, a claim that schools lie within a flood extent must be supported by registered school and flood layers and an executed spatial join. Final synthesis begins after the required dependencies are satisfied or remaining failures are identified. The Orchestrator reports the findings, references generated artifacts, and states limitations such as missing map features, partial imagery coverage, or failed operations. The resulting answer remains traceable to concrete geospatial outputs.

paragraphs.en: GeoFaham is implemented as a closed multi-agent team using a conversational agent framework ( Wu et al., 2024 ) , with custom orchestration, artifact storage, and geospatial execution layers. Vector outputs are stored as GeoJSON, raster outputs as Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs or derived layers, and imagery searches as registered item sets with temporal and band metadata. The file-backed, session-scoped Response Store supports reuse, recovery, and traceable handoffs. The implementation is model-agnostic. Models can be assigned to the planner, progress tracker, and specialists without changing the shared artifact interface, allowing stronger models to be reserved for planning, spatial query generation, and raster programming.

paragraphs.en: To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce GeoFaham-Bench, a benchmark containing 40 natural-language tasks across 17 real-world disaster records. The benchmark spans 10 task categories covering damage assessment, flood analysis, infrastructure and point-of-interest analysis, satellite imagery search, raster computation, spatial aggregation, and artifact generation. The task set emphasizes challenging multi-step workflows, with 24 of 40 tasks (60%) categorized as hard. We use the benchmark for two evaluations: an architecture-neutral comparison with external coding agents and a process-centric analysis of model assignments within GeoFaham. Detailed task and disaster statistics are provided in A.2 .
paragraphs.zh: 为了评估这些能力，我们提出了 GeoFaham-Bench，这是一个包含 40 项自然语言任务的基准，覆盖 17 个真实世界灾害记录。 该基准涵盖 10 个任务类别，包括损害评估、洪水分析、基础设施与兴趣点分析、卫星影像检索、栅格计算、空间聚合以及成果产物生成。 该任务集强调具有挑战性的多步骤工作流，其中 40 项任务中有 24 项（60%）被归类为困难任务。 我们使用该基准进行了两项评估：一是与外部智能体进行架构中立的对比，二是对 GeoFaham 内部模型分配进行以过程为中心的分析。 详细的任务与灾害统计信息见 A.2。

paragraphs.en: Tasks are written as user-facing disaster-response questions rather than tool-specific instructions, allowing systems to follow different valid workflows. They represent operational needs of GIS analysts, humanitarian workers, and government decision-makers, such as identifying exposed facilities, ranking damaged regions, retrieving event-relevant imagery, estimating affected area, or producing map artifacts. Task difficulty is defined by workflow complexity. Harder tasks require additional data sources, temporal reasoning, raster computation, or artifact handoffs. Each task also specifies the required evidence type, so reporting a statistic without a requested supporting artifact is considered incomplete.
paragraphs.zh: 任务以面向用户的灾害响应问题形式编写，而非针对特定工具的指令，从而使系统能够遵循不同的有效工作流程。 这些任务代表了 GIS 分析师、人道主义工作者和政府决策者的实际业务需求，例如识别暴露的设施、对受损区域进行排序、检索与事件相关的影像、估算受影响面积，或生成地图制品。 任务难度由工作流程的复杂程度定义。 更难的任务需要额外的数据源、时间推理、栅格计算或制品交接。 每个任务还指定了所需的证据类型，因此如果只报告统计数据而没有提供所要求的支持性制品，则视为不完整。

paragraphs.en: GeoFaham-Bench uses non-rigid ground truth that specifies required invariants, acceptable variations, expected-result checks, and common failure modes. This accommodates equivalent spatial predicates, execution orders, and raster-analysis thresholds, as well as small variations caused by dynamic sources such as OpenStreetMap and satellite catalogs. References are constructed through human-in-the-loop execution. For each task, a geospatial expert defines the disaster context, spatial and temporal scope, required evidence, and expected outputs. An LLM proposes a step-by-step workflow, tool calls, and implementation details, while the expert reviews each step and validates the intermediate results. Incorrect data sources, parameters, spatial operations, or outputs are corrected before proceeding. Corrections are limited to factual and validity errors, while the reasoning strategy and implementation choices remain with the system.
paragraphs.zh: GeoFaham-Bench 使用非刚性基准真值，该基准真值规定了所需的不变量、可接受的变化、预期结果检查以及常见失败模式。 这可以兼容等价的空间谓词、执行顺序和栅格分析阈值，以及由 OpenStreetMap 和卫星目录等动态源引起的微小变化。 参考答案通过人在回路的执行方式构建。 对于每个任务，一名地理空间专家定义灾害背景、空间和时间范围、所需证据以及预期输出。 大语言模型提出逐步的工作流程、工具调用和实现细节，而专家审查每个步骤并验证中间结果。 错误的数据源、参数、空间操作或输出会在继续之前得到纠正。 纠正仅限于事实性和有效性错误，而推理策略和实现选择仍由系统决定。

paragraphs.en: Task Outcome measures answer accuracy and completeness. paragraphs.en: Systems. We compare GeoFaham with three general-purpose coding-agent configurations: Codex with GPT-5.1 , Claude Code with Claude Sonnet 4.6 , and OpenCode with GPT-5.1 . All systems receive the same 40 benchmark tasks, source constraints, and geospatial execution environment. Each system may generate and execute code, queries, and tool calls to solve the tasks. For internal ablations, we evaluate four model-assignment configurations on the same tasks. C1 assigns GPT-4o to all roles. C2 upgrades only the Orchestrator planner to GPT-5.1. C3 additionally assigns GPT-5.1 to the progress tracker, Vector Agent, and Raster Agent, while retaining GPT-4o for the Maps and STAC agents. C4 assigns GPT-5.1 to all roles. For the cross-system comparison, GeoFaham uses the C3 tiered model assignment, with fresh runs conducted alongside the external coding agents under the same evaluation setup.9 We use GPT-5.2 as the LLM judge for both the cross-system and internal evaluation protocols.

paragraphs.en: Table 1 reports the aggregate results. GeoFaham achieves an overall score of 0.940, outperforming Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode by 6.1, 10.3, and 16.0 points, respectively. Codex is the strongest baseline with a score of 0.879. The largest category-level gains over Codex occur in task outcome, where GeoFaham scores 0.897 versus 0.794, and geospatial method, where it scores 0.951 versus 0.890. Compliance is high across all systems, indicating that agents generally follow instructions without violating benchmark rules. Figure 4 provides a dimension-level breakdown. The largest gains occur in spatial-temporal logic and data selection correctness. GeoFaham scores 0.918 and 0.972 on these dimensions, exceeding the strongest baseline by 13.9 and 11.9 points, respectively. These dimensions measure whether a system selects the correct evidence, preserves the intended spatial and temporal scope, and orders dependent operations correctly. In contrast, implementation correctness is comparable across systems: GeoFaham scores 0.922, while the strongest baseline scores 0.934. Geometry integrity is also consistently high, ranging from 0.956 to 0.997. These results indicate that GeoFaham’s advantage lies in selecting, coordinating, and validating geospatial operations rather than code generation alone. GeoFaham also achieves the highest artifact-quality score of 0.976, consistent with its artifact-aware execution and Response Store. Dimension-level scores are provided in the supplementary material.

paragraphs.en: Table 2 reports aggregate performance across the four internal configurations. C1, which assigns GPT-4o to all roles, achieves an overall score of 0.808. Upgrading only the Orchestrator planner in C2 raises the score to 0.914, an improvement of 10.6 points. This identifies planning as a major control point in the workflow. C3 additionally upgrades the progress tracker, Vector Agent, and Raster Agent while retaining GPT-4o for Maps and STAC. C3 achieves the highest mean score of 0.964, while C4, which assigns GPT-5.1 to every role, performs comparably with a score of 0.959. These results suggest that stronger models are most valuable in roles requiring planning, execution monitoring, spatial query generation, and raster programming. Constrained retrieval agents can use less expensive models without reducing overall performance. Dimension-level results further show that upgrading the planner primarily improves workflow construction and agent instructions, while stronger execution-oriented agents improve parameter accuracy, code logic, and final answer quality. Full per-dimension results are provided in the supplementary material.

paragraphs.en: Figure 5 distinguishes error occurrence from recovery. C1 encounters errors in 61.3% of runs and recovers 89.8% of them, resulting in 93.8% net success. C2 has the same error rate of 61.3%, but recovers all observed errors and achieves 100% net success. Here, net success denotes completion without an unrecovered execution error, not perfect benchmark correctness. This suggests upgrading the planner improves failure diagnosis and recovery, although it does not reduce errors. C3 and C4 reduce error occurrence to 33.8% and 28.8%, respectively, and recover all observed errors. Stronger execution-oriented agents therefore complement planning by preventing more failures before requiring recovery.
paragraphs.zh: 图5区分了错误的发生与恢复。 C1在61.3%的运行中遇到错误，并恢复了其中89.8%的错误，最终净成功率为93.8%。 C2的错误率同样是61.3%，但恢复了所有观察到的错误，实现了100%的净成功率。 这里，净成功指在没有未恢复的执行错误的情况下完成任务，而非基准测试的完全正确。 这表明升级规划器可以改善失败的诊断与恢复，尽管它并不能减少错误。 C3和C4分别将错误发生率降至33.8%和28.8%，并恢复了所有观察到的错误。 因此，更强的面向执行的智能体通过在需要恢复之前预防更多故障，对规划起到了补充作用。

paragraphs.en: Table 3 reports cross-system runtime and token usage. GeoFaham uses an average of 106,344 tokens per task, compared with 795,352 for Codex, 285,100 for Claude Code, and 376,042 for OpenCode. These values correspond to reductions of approximately 7.5 × 7.5\times , 2.7 × 2.7\times , and 3.5 × 3.5\times , respectively. paragraphs.en: We presented GeoFaham, a domain-specialized multi-agent system for geospatial disaster analytics. GeoFaham coordinates specialized agents for vector operations, map feature retrieval, imagery discovery, and raster analysis through validation-aware orchestration and artifact-preserving memory. We also introduced GeoFaham-Bench, a 40-task benchmark grounded in 17 real-world disaster records for evaluating multi-step geospatial reasoning, cross-source integration, and artifact generation under non-rigid evaluation. GeoFaham outperforms strong general-purpose coding-agent baselines, with the largest gains in data selection and spatial-temporal reasoning rather than implementation correctness. Internal ablations further show that strong models are most valuable for planning, progress tracking, spatial query generation, and raster analysis, while constrained retrieval roles can use less expensive models. These results highlight that reliable geospatial agents require not only executable code, but also explicit spatial and temporal grounding, validation of artifact dependencies, and persistent management of intermediate outputs.

paragraphs.en: GeoFaham-Bench includes disaster records spanning fires, floods, hurricanes, cyclones, earthquakes, and tornadoes across multiple geographic regions. The complete set of benchmark disaster records is listed in Table 4 . The hazard type provides the event context used to determine the relevant temporal window, area of interest, imagery selection, and downstream analysis requirements. For example, fire tasks may involve burn-severity analysis or aggregation of damaged buildings, flood tasks may require flood-footprint intersection and exposure analysis, and earthquake or storm tasks may focus on building damage and critical infrastructure impact. The authoritative disaster layers consist primarily of building-level damage assessments, flood-extent maps, or both. OpenStreetMap features and satellite imagery are retrieved separately to support additional spatial and temporal analysis. The benchmark also covers different regions and administrative structures, introducing variation in place names, boundary availability, and OpenStreetMap coverage. The selected events are recent enough to support satellite-imagery searches over event-centered temporal windows. For each disaster record, we prepare supporting context for task design, including the area of interest, event metadata, available damage or flood layers, relevant map-feature inventories, and a short event overview. paragraphs.en: Difficulty is defined by workflow complexity rather than answer length. Simple tasks require one data source and direct retrieval or aggregation, medium tasks require two sources or a spatial operation, and hard tasks require three or more sources, temporal reasoning, raster computation, or artifact handoff between intermediate stages. Of the 40 tasks, 24 (60%) are hard, 12 (30%) are medium, and 4 (10%) are simple, emphasizing multi-step workflows over direct retrieval. Two tasks are explicitly multi-turn, comprising four follow-up turns in total. Each task also specifies the expected evidence type, including textual statistics, GeoJSON layers, raster outputs, tables, or combined artifacts.

paragraphs.en: For each benchmark task, the validated ground truth is represented as a structured specification containing the disaster context, area of interest, event date, target feature type, buffer distance, temporal window, expected data sources, required spatial predicates, CRS constraints, expected output type, acceptable numerical tolerances, and known failure modes. This specification defines the spatial, temporal, methodological, and output-level conditions that a valid solution must satisfy, without requiring systems to reproduce a single implementation. The cross-system judge evaluates each run using the evidence exposed by that system. For GeoFaham, this includes run metadata, conversation history, agent messages, Response Store entries, and generated artifacts. For external coding agents, it includes the task prompt, stdout, stderr, structured result output, generated files, scripts, SQL, and workspace artifacts. Failed or timed-out runs are evaluated using the evidence produced before failure, allowing supported intermediate results to receive partial credit while penalizing unsupported or hallucinated claims. The evaluation also checks geospatial-specific failure modes, including selection of the wrong evidence source, misidentification of the disaster or area of interest, violation of event-date constraints, inappropriate spatial predicates, and metric computations performed without a suitable projected CRS or geodesic method. Geometry-derived values must be traceable to deterministic spatial engines such as PostGIS, GeoPandas, Shapely, GDAL, or rasterio; values inferred directly from coordinate text are penalized regardless of numerical plausibility. The judge additionally records diagnostic flags for run completion, structured-output validity, timeout, missing artifacts, forbidden-source usage, unsupported claims, and inappropriate CRS usage. These flags support failure-mode analysis independently of the aggregate score.
paragraphs.zh: 对于每个基准任务，经过验证的地面真值以结构化规范表示，其中包含灾害背景、感兴趣区域、事件日期、目标要素类型、缓冲距离、时间窗口、预期数据源、所需空间谓词、坐标系约束、预期输出类型、可接受的数值容差以及已知失败模式。 该规范定义了有效解必须满足的空间、时间、方法与输出层面的条件，但不要求系统复现单一实现。 跨系统评审器使用每个系统所暴露的证据来评估每次运行。 对于 GeoFaham，这包括运行元数据、对话历史、智能体消息、响应存储条目以及生成的产物。 对于外部编码智能体，这包括任务提示、标准输出、标准错误、结构化结果输出、生成的文件、脚本、SQL 以及工作区产物。 失败或超时的运行使用失败前产生的证据进行评估，从而允许有依据的中间结果获得部分分数，同时对无依据或虚构的声明进行惩罚。 评估还检查地理空间特有的失败模式，包括选择错误的证据来源、误判灾害或感兴趣区域、违反事件日期约束、使用不当的空间谓词，以及在没有合适投影坐标系或测地线方法的情况下进行度量计算。 由几何推导的数值必须可追溯到确定性的空间引擎，如 PostGIS、GeoPandas、Shapely、GDAL 或 rasterio；直接从坐标文本推断出的数值，无论其数值上看似多么合理，都会受到惩罚。 评审器还会记录关于运行完成情况、结构化输出有效性、超时、缺失产物、使用禁用来源、无依据声明以及坐标系使用不当的诊断标记。 这些标记支持独立于总分的失败模式分析。

paragraphs.zh: 两种评估协议均按五分制对每个维度打分：1.00 表示结果正确、完整且论据充分；0.75 表示结果基本正确但存在少量遗漏；0.50 表示部分正确但存在重要缺口；0.25 表示存在重大缺陷但仍有一些有用的证据；0.00 表示结果缺失、缺乏支持、不正确或不符合要求。 当替代工作流满足相同的、经验证的空间、时间、方法以及输出层面的要求时，可获得满分。
